questions.q: What algorithm does an induction head implement?
options: It always attends only to the very first token in a sequence
It deletes repeated tokens from the input
Given the current token, find an earlier occurrence of that same token and predict whatever token followed it that previous time: `[A][B] ... [A] -> predict [B]`
It predicts the next token purely from positional information, ignoring token identity entirely
questions.explain: This is the induction algorithm: search the context for an earlier occurrence of the current token, then copy forward whatever followed it.

questions.q: How many heads, and in what arrangement, implement the induction algorithm according to Olsson, Elhage et al. (2022)?
options: Every attention head in the model simultaneously
A single head acting entirely alone
An entire transformer block dedicated solely to induction
Two heads in different layers: an earlier-layer previous token head writes information the later-layer induction head reads and uses
questions.explain: It's a two-head circuit: a previous token head feeds information into the residual stream that the induction head, in a later layer, reads and uses to find and copy the earlier pattern.

questions.q: What does the previous token head specifically contribute to this circuit?
options: It has no functional role in the circuit
It attends from each position to the position right before it and writes "what token came right before me" into the residual stream, for the induction head to read later
It directly predicts the final output token on its own
It deletes all information about earlier tokens
questions.explain: The previous token head's job is purely to make 'what came before this position' available in the residual stream, which the induction head in a later layer then reads.

questions.q: What training-dynamics finding did the paper report that supports treating induction heads as actually responsible for in-context learning?
options: Induction heads form only after training is fully complete
In-context learning ability increases perfectly smoothly throughout training with no notable events
A sudden phase transition early in training, where in-context learning ability jumps sharply at almost the same point induction heads first form
There is no relationship between induction head formation and in-context learning ability
questions.explain: The coincidence between the phase transition in in-context learning and the formation of induction heads is strong evidence this specific circuit drives the behavior.

questions.q: In the repeated-sequence test code, what does a high `induction_score` indicate?
options: That the model's predictions during the repeated half of the sequence consistently match the pattern established in the first half, consistent with induction-like behavior
That the model has zero attention heads
That the vocabulary size is too small for meaningful testing
That the model has memorized its training data verbatim
questions.explain: A high score means the model's predictions during the repeat line up with what actually followed each token the first time, which is the behavioral signature of induction -- though confirming it's specifically this circuit still requires head-level analysis.
